title: Shaquille O’Neal’s Advice for NBA Phenom Victor Wembanyama: ‘Be Meaner’
description:
Shaquille O’Neal’s second act has been full of surprises.

	The NBA legend and cultural icon has served as a sheriff’s deputy, reserve officer and
body:
Shaquille O’Neal’s second act has been full of surprises.

	The NBA legend and cultural icon has served as a sheriff’s deputy, reserve officer and honorary U.S. Marshal, at one point helping the Justice Department track down internet predators online; earned two master’s degrees and a doctorate; accumulated (and sold) 155 fast food franchises and 40 gyms; briefly co-owned the Sacramento Kings; runs the popular Dunkman slam-dunk league; tours the country as a DJ; and recently popped up in the new “Scary Movie.” Shaq’s also in his 15th season as one of the hosts of “Inside the NBA,” the “greatest sports studio show in the history of television,” according to The New York Times.
	

	And yet, despite his considerable on-court accomplishments — four NBA championships, three NBA Finals MVPs, 15 All-Star selections and status as the most dominant big man of the modern era — Shaq rarely finds himself in the GOAT conversation, which typically pits Michael Jordan against LeBron James. When asked if this bothers him at all, Shaq launches into a story about his youth.


	“The answer is yes and no,” he tells Variety. “I could remember crying to my mom one day about being the best athlete in my high school, but I didn’t win Athlete of the Year. My mom grabbed me and said, ‘Baby, nobody roots for Goliath.’ And I said, ‘What does that mean?’ And she said, ‘When you’re big, they expect you to do certain things, but the little guy will always get the praise.’”

	He continues: “And I’m seeing it now because when you’re talking about the GOATs, it doesn’t matter who you pick, but please mention Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Yet they always go for the little guy — ‘Ooh Mike,’ ‘Ooh Kobe,’ ‘Ooh LeBron.’ So, do I feel underappreciated? Yes. But nobody roots for Goliath. And I’m flattered when a lot of people talk about their best big men and my name is mentioned, and when it comes to the most dominant ever then my name is one of two.”
	

	Through his production company Jersey Legends, Shaq has spearheaded a number of TV projects, from the aforementioned Dunkman league to the acclaimed “Allen Iv3rson” docuseries for Prime, the Netflix reality show “Power Moves With Shaquille O’Neal” and a number of other scripted projects in development.

	One thing you won’t see Shaq touch, however, is a documentary on his former Lakers teammate Kobe Bryant.

	“I wouldn’t want to do one because that enigmatic, legendary story’s been told,” he explains. “If I was asked to do it by his family then I would do it, but I’m not just going to do it to be doing it.”

	With the 2026-27 NBA season tipping off Oct. 20, one thing Shaq would like to see is more fire from Victor Wembanyama, the towering 22-year-old phenom whose San Antonio Spurs were felled in the NBA Finals by the New York Knicks. He says he enjoyed when Wemby threw Knicks superstar Jalen Brunson to the ground by the back of his head during the Finals and would like to see a lot more of that from the spindly Frenchman.

	“I like Wemby, and that was a mean moment, but I’d like you to be mean all the time,” offers Shaq. “When things are difficult, I like breaking it down to its simplest form. It’s difficult to shoot a lot of threes and hit a lot of threes in high-pressure games, so when you’re 7’5”, you have to take advantage of your skill set. There’s no way a coach should even have the guts to say, ‘[Alex] Caruso, when you switch on him, play him.’ I would like him to read and react a little bit different. I’m not saying be a post guy, but when a guy on you is smaller than you, I don’t think you should shoot a jumper ever.”

	A moment that really got under Shaq’s skin as a big man who was unstoppable in the low block was when the Knicks’ Jose Alvarado, all 6’0” of him, bodied up on Wemby in the Finals.

	“Jose is my guy, but you need to put your arm around Jose and bash his face into the ground so he knows, ‘OK, if you’re gonna try to box me out, then I’m going to put this elbow in the back of your neck every time,’” Shaq says. “But other than that, fabulous player, great shooter and definitely has all the tools. If you’re playing for a historical franchise such as the Spurs, you’re going to have to win at some point. They almost had it, but I need him to be meaner.”

schema.headline: Shaquille O’Neal’s Advice for NBA Phenom Victor Wembanyama: ‘Be Meaner’

title: WGA East Strikes Deal With Cloak to Safeguard Screenplays from AI Scraping
description: The Writers Guild of America East has struck a partnership with the AI shielding tool Cloak, a service that aims to help writers safeguard their wo
body:
The Writers Guild of America East has struck a partnership with the AI shielding tool Cloak, a service that aims to help writers safeguard their work from training AI models.

	The partnership will provide WGAE members with free access to Cloak, while non-WGAE members can pay $10 for Cloak once they register their script with the guild. Cloak’s software makes a script resistant to scraping by most AI models while preserving its formatting, making it harder for those models to train on writers’ work. 
	

	The effort responds to years of training from those models on screenplays without explicit permission, which has sparked questions over the legality of using those scripts without permission. The union has maintained that using scripts to train AI models does not constitute fair use.


	“The WGAE partnership with Cloak expands our efforts to protect members’ work and fight back against AI companies exploiting writers and other creative workers,” WGAE president Tom Fontana said in a statement. “We’re excited about the partnership with Cloak because it means members don’t need to worry that their work will be used to train AI models after they send it to producers or agents – or simply that the product of weeks, months, or years of work will be reduced to an AI-generated summary of an email attachment.”

	“For the past 3 years, the assumption was that anything you put out onto the internet is at risk of being ingested by AI, so I developed Cloak as a way to give agency back to writers to protect against unwanted AI training, AI notes, and analysis,” Cloak founder Rishi Ambavanekar added. “Until now, there hasn’t been a real technically-sound way to fight back against AI and determine how the content you create actually interacts with it. I hope Cloak can keep creative writing in the hands of people and not as data being processed by machines. I want to thank the WGAE and look forward to seeing writers have more confidence in sharing their work far and wide.”
	

	The deal came as part of the WGAE’s AI efforts, which include an AI task force. Larry J. Cohen, the co-chair of the task force, said the deal represented a “natural and necessary extension of our fight to protect our members’ creative rights and the integrity of their work.”

	““Generative AI models are often falsely advertised on the promise that they will make our work obsolete, but the truth is, the creative process is human and always will be,” Cohen added. “That’s why the Guild is advocating for better protections against and awareness of the risks posed by AI – not just through our contracts, but through legislation and member education.”

	The WGAE has been broadly resistant to the incorporation of AI into the filmmaking process. The guild ended its 12-year partnership with Urbanworld, the BIPOC-focused film festival, in July over the festival’s decision to introduce a programming lane for AI-generated films and shorts. It also launched an #AINeedsHumans campaign to mobilize its members around the technology’s improper use, and it made AI a pillar of its negotiations with Hollywood studios during its 148-day strike in 2023.

schema.headline: WGA East Strikes Deal With Cloak to Safeguard Screenplays from AI Scraping

title: ‘Deadstream’ Directors Joseph and Vanessa Winter to Helm Horror Movie ‘Future Me’ as Longevity Pictures, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios Ink Multi-Picture Deal (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Deadstream” helmers Joseph and Vanessa Winter are set to direct horror-thriller “Future Me,” based on a viral Reddit short story by Daria Vasileva
body:
“Deadstream” helmers Joseph and Vanessa Winter are set to direct horror-thriller “Future Me,” based on a viral Reddit short story by Daria Vasileva. The film is the first title of a multi-picture deal between L.A. and UAE-based production company Longevity Pictures, indie genre label Spooky Pictures and Abu Dhabi’s Image Nation Studios.

	Originally published in the “NoSleep” subreddit — the online community dedicated to user-generated horror fiction — “Future Me” follows a man “who receives a deeply unsettling email from his past self via the ‘FutureMe’ website, a message that draws him down a terrifying and increasingly surreal rabbit hole,” according to its synopsis.
	

	“Deadstream” was the first feature by the husband-and-wife filmmaking team. The horror comedy premiered at SXSW in 2022 before being acquired by Shudder, where it became one of the genre streaming platform’s most acclaimed original releases. They followed that success by directing the fan-favorite segment “To Hell and Back” in found-footage horror anthology film “V/H/S/99.”


	Joseph and Vanessa Winter’s next project is the previously announced film “Amityville,” a radical new spin on the Amityville Horror franchise, based on Jay Anson’s book that was published in 1977 about the paranormal experiences of the George Lutz family. The book led to nine films between 1979 and 2005. “Amityville” is being produced by Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath of Divide/Conquer and Raphael Margules and J.D. Lifshitz, principals of genre-focused production label BoulderLight Pictures.

	Joseph and Vanessa Winter’s upcoming “Future Me” will instead be produced by Majd Nassif (“Mercy”) for Longevity Pictures, alongside Steven Schneider (“Late Night With the Devil”) and Roy Lee (“Weapons,” “Barbarian”) for Spooky Pictures. Image Nation Studios’ Ben Ross (“Watcher,” “Late Night With the Devil”) and Longevity Pictures’ Aysel Lyatifova, (“Six Till Midnight”) will executive produce.
	

	“Future Me” follows the initial collaboration between Longevity Pictures, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios on upcoming horror thriller “Home Safety Hotline” directed by Michael Matthews (“Love and Monsters”) and based on Night Signal Entertainment’s popular puzzle video game of the same name. Other titles on their multi-picture slate remain to be unveiled.

	“Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios have built an incredible track record for championing high-concept, creator-driven horror storytelling, so expanding our partnership felt like a natural next step,” Nassif said in a statement. 

	“After the success of ‘Backrooms,’ the potential of internet lore as fertile ground for adaptation has become undeniable,” he went on to note. “So we’re excited to be bringing ‘Future Me’ to life with a team which shares our passion for original and punchy genre projects.”

	Commented Spooky Pictures’ Steven Schneider and Image Nation Studios’ Ben Ross: “Longevity Pictures brings exactly the kind of creative flair and commercial instinct that we champion, so we’re thrilled to be building a slate together that combines killer storytelling with strong commercial appeal.”

	“Horror filmmaking is firing on all cylinders right now, with both audiences and critics embracing fresh concepts and emerging creative voices, making this the ideal time to bring more genre films to audiences worldwide,” they added. “‘Future Me” is exactly the kind of project we’re looking to get behind — a chilling premise with a passionate existing fanbase, and with Joseph and Vanessa Winter on board, it has all the makings of a standout horror film.”

schema.headline: ‘Deadstream’ Directors Joseph and Vanessa Winter to Helm Horror Movie ‘Future Me’ as Longevity Pictures, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios Ink Multi-Picture Deal (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Patrick Dempsey Signs With Gersh (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Patrick Dempsey has signed with Gersh for representation.

	The Emmy and Golden Globe Award-nominated actor is a big get for the company, which is
body:
Patrick Dempsey has signed with Gersh for representation.

	The Emmy and Golden Globe Award-nominated actor is a big get for the company, which is the fourth largest talent and literary agency in the world.

	Dempsey currently stars in and executive produces the Fox series “Memory of a Killer,” which streams on Hulu. Season 2 of the drama is currently in production in Toronto, with filming expected to wrap at the end of the year.


	Dempsey is, of course, best known for his portrayal of Dr. Derek Shepherd aka “McDreamy” on ABC’s “Grey’s Anatomy,” which earned him two Golden Globe nominations and a Screen Actors Guild Award as part of the ensemble cast. Dempsey appeared in 262 episodes across 12 seasons of the medical procedural, leaving midway through Season 11 in 2014 and then coming back for a run of episodes six years later, in Season 17.
	

	Dempsey, he himself a race car driver, also starred in Michael Mann’s biopic “Ferrari” opposite Adam Driver and Penélope Cruz, as well as Eli Roth’s “Thanksgiving.” He is also known for his romantic lead turn opposite Amy Adams in 2007’s “Enchanted,” and he reprised the role in the 2022 sequel, “Disenchanted.”

	On the small screen, Dempsey recently starred as Captain Aaron Spencer in “Dexter: Original Sin.” His additional television credits include the international drama series “Devils” and the limited series “The Truth About the Harry Quebert Affair.”

	Dempsey first rose to prominence with “Can’t Buy Me Love” and “Loverboy,” and his additional film credits include “Sweet Home Alabama,” “Made of Honor,” “Bridget Jones’s Baby,” “Transformers: Dark of the Moon,” “Valentine’s Day,” “Freedom Writers” and “Scream 3.”
	

	In 2023, Dempsey was bestowed the great honor of People’s Sexiest Man Alive.

	He continues to be represented by attorney Mitch Smelkinson.

title: ‘Sinners’ Music Exhibition Opens at California African American Museum
description:
An exhibition dedicated to the music of Ryan Coogler’s Oscar-winning “Sinners” has opened at the California African American Museum.

	“Sinners: So
body:
An exhibition dedicated to the music of Ryan Coogler’s Oscar-winning “Sinners” has opened at the California African American Museum.

	“Sinners: Sounds That Summon” is on view Oct. 20-March 14. Presented in collaboration with Warner Bros. Archives, the presentation is the first museum exhibition devoted to film’s music.

	“Sound has the power to form creative worlds that manifest joy, protection, belonging and freedom,” reads an official description of the show. “‘Sinners: Sounds That Summon’ revisits the fan-favorite Club Juke sequence, in which music acts as a portal through time, from traditional African ritual to present-day street dance. Centered around the guitar used by protagonist Sammie ‘Preacher Boy’ Moore, the exhibition brings together costumes, objects and archival material from the film to consider how Black music carries memory, movement, style and spirit across generations.”
	

	“Sinners” follows twin brothers (both played by Michael B. Jordan) in 1932 fighting evil supernatural forces when they return home to the Mississippi Delta. The cast also includes Hailee Steinfeld, Miles Caton, Jack O’Connell, Wunmi Mosaku, Jayme Lawson, Omar Benson Miller, Li Jun Li and Delroy Lindo. The film was nominated for 16 Oscars at the 98th Academy Awards, the most of any film in history. It took home four Oscars: best actor (Jordan), original screenplay (Coogler), cinematography (Autumn Durald Arkapaw) and original score (Ludwig Göransson).


	“Sounds That Summon” uses music as the thread that weaves together three themes: Music Makes Sound, Music Makes Movement and Music Makes Worlds. Music Makes Sound looks at instruments through the traditions and histories they carry. Music Makes Movement examines dance as an embodied form of cultural memory, tracing how movement transforms and traverses generations and communities. Music Makes Worlds considers how music extends beyond sound to create language, fashion, identity and community. Alongside Sammie’s guitar, visitors will encounter objects, costumes and props used in the film, including Smoke and Stack’s costumes and the Club Juke sign, evoking the feeling of stepping into the juke joint itself.
	

	The exhibition culminates in Sounds That Carry Us, a participatory experience inspired by the contrast between the joy, safety and collective freedom experienced inside Club Juke and the isolation and danger outside of it. Visitors will be asked to reflect on a song, sound, or genre that carries them back to joy, hope, freedom or community. “Sinners: Sounds That Summon” is co-organized by CAAM and Warner Bros. Archives and curated by Imani Y. Haynes.

schema.headline: ‘Sinners’ Music Exhibition Opens at California African American Museum

title: Daniel Kaluuya to Star in ‘Purpose’ Playwright Branden Jacobs-Jenkins’ Next Show ‘Grass’
description:
Daniel Kaluuya will make his New York stage debut in “Grass,” a new play from Tony Award- and Pulitzer Prize-winner Branden Jacobs-Jenkins.

	“Gras
body:
Daniel Kaluuya will make his New York stage debut in “Grass,” a new play from Tony Award- and Pulitzer Prize-winner Branden Jacobs-Jenkins.

	“Grass” traces a mother and son’s surreal, sprawling road trip through the American South marked by fantastical encounters with historical and allegorical figures. A press release describes “Grass” as “equal parts fantasia, memory play, and morality play” and a “surreal meditation on the limits of personal, ancestral, and national identity amidst social upheaval.” The play will have its world premiere Off Broadway at Park Avenue Armory, with opening night set for Feb. 26. 
	

	Jacob-Jenkins is the playwright behind Broadway hits including “Appropriate,” which starred Sarah Paulson, Corey Stoll, Natalie Gold, Elle Fanning and Alyssa Emily Marvin, and “Purpose,” led by Jon Michael Hill, LaTanya Richardson Jackson, Harry Lennix and Kara Young. “Appropriate” was nominated for eight Tonys and won three, including best revival. “Purpose” was nominated for six Tonys and won two, including best play.


	Kaluuya won an Oscar for Shaka King’s 2021 Fred Hampton biopic “Judas and the Black Messiah.” The British actor broke out in 2017’s Oscar-nominated “Get Out” and went on to star in movies such as “Black Panther,” Steve McQueen’s crime drama “Widows,” Jordan Peele’s “Nope,” Sony’s “Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse” and Chris Rock’s “Mistry Green.” He’s also currently developing a live-action “Barney” movie for A24 and Mattel. On stage, Kaluuya appeared in several London productions including “Oxford Street,” “Sucker Punch,” “A Season in the Congo” and “Blue/Orange.”
	

	“Grass” reunites Jacobs-Jenkins with director Sarah Benson and set designer Mimi Lien, who worked on his 2014 play “An Octoroon.” The creative team includes lighting designer Jane Cox and Stacey Derosier, sound designer Bray Poor, special effects designer Jeremy Chernick, costume designer Enver Chakartash and wig and makeup designer Cookie Jordan.

schema.headline: Daniel Kaluuya to Star in ‘Purpose’ Playwright Branden Jacobs-Jenkins’ Next Show ‘Grass’

title: Robert Pattinson Was Bribed to Star in ‘Primetime’ With 200 Zyn Canisters and a Note That Read: ‘Dear Chris Han-Zyn’
description:
How do you get an A-list actor to star in your movie? If it’s Robert Pattinson, the answer is a whole lot of nicotine.

	The “Batman” and “Odyssey”
body:
How do you get an A-list actor to star in your movie? If it’s Robert Pattinson, the answer is a whole lot of nicotine.

	The “Batman” and “Odyssey” star is generating Oscar buzz for his portrayal of “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen in A24’s “Primetime.” But Pattinson was originally planning to stay behind the camera, serving only as a producer.

	That is until “Primetime” screenwriter Ajon Singh retooled the script to convince Pattinson to take the lead role, while director Lance Oppenheim thought of a brilliant bribe.
	

	“Rob, at the time, was grappling with a Zyn addiction,” Oppenheim told Vulture, referring to the nicotine pouch brand. There was a Zyn shortage in the U.S. at the time, so Oppenheim recruited a friend in Canada to send 200 canisters to Pattinson’s home in Los Angeles. Then, Oppenheim dropped off the latest draft of “Primetime” with a letter that began, “Dear Chris Han-Zyn.”


	Pattinson called the director after reading the new script and said he would take the role. Said Oppenheim, “It was like LeBron making the announcement that he was joining the Heat.”

	“Primetime” opened on Sept. 25 and landed on the higher end of box office expectations, raking in nearly $50 million worldwide against a $15 million production budget. The film also caught the attention of Hansen himself, who has lashed out against the movie and Pattinson’s performance as a “complete work of fiction.” Hansen’s review was an anomaly; critics generally rallied behind the film, with Variety‘s Owen Gleiberman calling Pattinson a “new kind of movie star” with “nervy dyspeptic magnetism.” “He’s a star for the age of entropy,” Gleiberman wrote, “for an era when everything is falling apart.”

schema.headline: Robert Pattinson Was Bribed to Star in ‘Primetime’ With 200 Zyn Canisters and a Note That Read: ‘Dear Chris Han-Zyn’

title: JustWatch TV Launches With Content Partners Including Cineverse and Altitude for New AVOD Streaming Service
description: Streaming guide JustWatch Group set its 30 major content partners for its Advertising-Based Video on Demand streaming service, JustWatch TV, which
body:
Streaming guide JustWatch Group set its 30 major content partners for its Advertising-Based Video on Demand streaming service, JustWatch TV, which launched Tuesday.

	Cineverse will serve as the content partner in the U.S. alongside Leonine Studios in Germany, SND in France and Altitude in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The companies join previously announced partners Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street and Vortex Media.
	

	“The launch of JustWatch TV marks the most important new development in our company’s 12-year history, and it’s only the start,” says David Croyé, the founder and CEO of the JustWatch Group. “We called our company JustWatch because we wanted to make it easier for people to find and ‘just watch’ the movies and shows they love. From the beginning, our vision was to create a single platform that directs fans to all of their entertainment options in one place. JustWatch TV will help fill in the gaps and will make it easier for the massive JustWatch audience to discover and watch great movies and series, including those hard-to-find titles, right from the app itself.”


	Available directly through the JustWatch apps and website, the streaming service offers free, rental and ad-free subscription options across 11 markets: the U.S., Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain, Australia and New Zealand.

	JustWatch TV uses a model that enables viewers to watch media both directly on the platform or on their preferred streaming services. The streaming service also includes “Why to Watch” features, which analyzes data on what audiences are wanting to watch..
	

	JustWatch Group is the operator of the world’s largest streaming guide, reaching 50 million global consumers.

schema.headline: JustWatch TV Launches With Content Partners Including Cineverse and Altitude for New AVOD Streaming Service

title: ‘MobLand’ Actor Mandeep Dhillon to Star in Self-Written Short ‘The Things I Want to Do to You’ Alongside Golda Rosheuvel and Scott Karim (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
“MobLand” actor Mandeep Dhillon has started production on short “The Things I Want to Do to You,” which she wrote and will star in.

	Directed by B
body:
“MobLand” actor Mandeep Dhillon has started production on short “The Things I Want to Do to You,” which she wrote and will star in.

	Directed by BAFTA nominee Lynette Linton, the psychological drama also features “Bridgerton” star Golda Rosheuvel and “The Game’s” Scott Karim. It’s produced by Katie Glaister under Dhillon’s production banner Hazy Plant Pictures Ltd., marking the company’s first project.


	“The Things I Want to Do to You” explores “rage, revenge, trauma and the complexities of seeking justice,” according to its official synopsis. The short film “follows a woman navigating the aftermath of a deeply personal violation. Through a series of increasingly provocative fantasies, she confronts the things she wishes she could do to the man responsible. Blurring the lines between imagination and reality, the film examines the anger women are often forced to carry in silence and what happens when that anger finally demands to be heard.”
	

	“I’ve always been fascinated by the things we think but never say out loud, particularly when we’ve been wronged,” Dhillon said in a statement. “The anger, the grief, the fantasies of revenge and the conversations we have in our heads that will never happen in real life. I think so many women carry the weight of injustice, often in silence. I wanted to explore that space between what we feel, what we imagine and what we actually do. The darker, sometimes outrageous, places our minds can go when we feel powerless. At its heart, this film is about giving a voice to those unspoken emotions and exploring what it means to carry something you never asked for.”
	

	“The Things I Want to Do to You” is currently filming in the U.K., with other cast members including Arabella Coombes, Eisa Latif and Saher Shah.

	Dhillon added, “To be bringing this story to life alongside Lynette Linton, Golda Rosheuvel and such an incredible team is something I’m immensely proud of. As the first production from my company, Hazy Plant Pictures, it feels particularly special, and I couldn’t be more excited for this to mark the beginning of our journey.”

schema.headline: ‘MobLand’ Actor Mandeep Dhillon to Star in Self-Written Short ‘The Things I Want to Do to You’ Alongside Golda Rosheuvel and Scott Karim (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Alex Cooper Gives Birth To First Child with Husband Matt Kaplan
description:
Alex Cooper
                          Call Me Mommy 'Cause My Baby is Here!!!
body:
Alex Cooper
                          Call Me Mommy 'Cause My Baby is Here!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 20, 2026
                            6:56 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Call her officially a mommy ... because Alex Cooper has given birth to her first baby!!!
      
    
            The "Call Her Daddy" podcast host shared the news on her Instagram Tuesday morning, posting her newborn in a cozy mint green outfit and captioning the post with a blue heart ... seemingly revealing she gave birth to a boy.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Alex announced she was expecting her first child with hubby Matt Kaplan back in May, showing off her baby bump and captioning the post "Our family."
      

            The CEO of "The Unwell Network" has kept the Daddy Gang up to date along her journey as a first-time mother, and has even given back to many of her fans by completely clearing out their baby registries as a thank you for advice.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Unlike her highly public career, Cooper and Kaplan have kept their relationship mostly under wraps. The two were first linked in 2020 after meeting through mutual connections in the entertainment industry, and their romance gradually blossomed away from the public eye.
      
    
            Now, all eyes are on the new family of three as they gear up to pass their little one the podcast mic.

title: Russell Brand Accuser Details 'Violent' Alleged Sexual Assault at Rape Trial
description:
Russell Brand Rape Trial
                          Accuser Describes 'Frenzied,' 'Violent' Allege
body:
Russell Brand Rape Trial
                          Accuser Describes 'Frenzied,' 'Violent' Alleged Sexual Assault
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 20, 2026
                            7:17 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A woman who claims Russell Brand sexually assaulted her took the stand on Tuesday in his rape trial ... describing the alleged incident as "frenzied" and even "violent" ... and she claims his entourage stood by and watched.
      
    
            The woman testified in court that she was working at a radio station in London in the mid-2000s when he grabbed her suddenly and allegedly began kissing her.
      
    
            Brand allegedly grabbed the woman's buttocks and breasts and pushed her against a wall ... and she says 4 members of his entourage -- 3 men and 1 woman -- watched the "violent," "sloppy" and "frenzied" alleged attack.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The woman says she eventually pushed him away and told him to "f*** off" ... after which she says Brand backed off and began laughing.
      
    
            The incident was no laughing matter to the woman, though ... who went outside to smoke a cigarette, feeling "dirty, shocked, stunned and shaken.”
      
    
            The alleged victim did not go to the cops at the time ... but reported the incident in 2023. When asked if she is sure Brand is the one who assaulted her, the woman replied, "The person who assaulted me was Russell Brand. I can't forget that.”
      
    
            As for why she didn't tell her employer, Capital Radio, the woman says the company culture was misogynistic ... and she felt her colleagues would just tell her she was "lucky." She also said she feared losing her job and had a mortgage to pay.
      
    
            As we've reported ... other women have also detailed their own alleged experiences with Brand in court -- with one claiming he raped her in her hotel room and another alleging he tried to pull her into a bathroom while working for MTV.
      
    
            Brand has repeatedly denied all wrongdoing ... insisting he has never had nonconsensual sex with anyone.
      
    
            He is facing 7 charges ... three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault.

title: Model Sahara Ray Dead at 34

            Sahara Ray, the Australian model and swimwear designer who once made headlines for her rumored relationship with Justin Bieber, has died ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            "She passed away last night surrounded by family at the hospital. She was so loved," Sahara's family tells TMZ.
      
    
            Her cause of death has not been confirmed.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Ray rose to fame through her modeling career and social media presence, building a massive following on Instagram while launching her own swimwear brand, Sahara Ray Swim.
      

            She made headlines in 2016 when she was photographed vacationing with Bieber in Hawaii. She was also previously romantically linked to Australian singer Cody Simpson.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The model was the daughter of legendary Australian surfer Tony Ray and spent much of her childhood traveling between Australia, California and Hawaii.
      
    
            In 2024, Sahara opened up about her battle with Guillain-Barré syndrome -- a rare neurological disorder that left her partially paralyzed following a serious car accident.
      
    
            She was 34.
      
    
            RIP
